generated.title: Paragraph exceeds 10 lines and covers multiple unrelated ideas
generated.description: The paragraph beginning 'In their paper Interactive Learning…' spans from page 2 into page 3, making it well over 10 rendered lines. It also compresses at least three distinct ideas into a single paragraph: (a) the interactive learning concept and its purpose, (b) the specific shortening of the theory-practice gap, and (c) the lecture phase structure (theory, example, practice, sample solution, feedback, reflection) and its connection to Artemis. This paragraph should be split into two or three shorter paragraphs, each developing one idea.

locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory, which is usually taught in the non-interactive lecture, and practice, which typically follows about a week later, so that less knowledge is lost [Krusche17]. The concept, called Interactive learning, makes it possible for students to transfer the new acquired skills to real, application-based use cases still during lecture [Krusche17]. In order to implement this idea, the lecture is **split up**

**into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].**

For example, in the Abstract, Jenkins is called both an "external CI server" and part of "external applications" to migrate "the CI service." In the Problem Statement, it is a "CI server," while in the Proposed Solution it becomes a "CI system" and then a "CI service." Since this is the core concept of the proposal, a single consistent term (e.g., "CI server" for standalone systems and "CI service" only when specifically referring to the integrated GitLab CI component) should be used throughout the author's own prose.

locations.quote: migrate the **CI service** from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt **CI service**
The interactive learning platform Artemis currently only supports setups with an external **CI server**
Artemis currently supports Bamboo and Jenkins as a **CI server** for executing the tests
a **CI system** not storing each build plan individually
the **CI service** should be part of the VC server to reduce additional efort

kept.title: Inconsistent terminology: "task" vs "exercise"
kept.description: The Abstract uses "task" ("after the task has been assigned") while the rest of the document consistently uses "exercise" to denote the same concept (e.g., "after the student started the exercise," "release of an exercise," "start exercise button"). Since "exercise" is the established term in the Artemis context and used throughout the body, the Abstract should also use "exercise" for consistency.
